readings.title: The Messengers of Elohim
readings.subtitle: Ya‛aqoḇ establishes his camp and initiates contact with Ěsav.
readings.text: [Genesis 32:1] And Ya‛aqoḇ went on his way, and the messengers of <dn>Elohim</dn> met him. [2] And when Ya‛aqoḇ saw them, he said, “This is the camp of <dn>Elohim</dn>.” And he called the name of that place Maḥanayim. [3] And Ya‛aqoḇ sent messengers before him to Ěsav his brother in the land of Sě‛ir, the field of Eḏom [4] and he commanded them, saying, “Say this to my master Ěsav, ‘Your servant Ya‛aqoḇ said this, “I have sojourned with Laḇan and stayed there until now. [5] “And I have bulls, and donkeys, flocks, and male and female servants. And I have sent to inform my master, to find favour in your eyes.” ’ ”

readings.title: Ya‛aqoḇ Pleads the Covenant Promise
readings.subtitle: Facing the threat of Ra, Ya‛aqoḇ leans his full weight upon YeHoVaH's guarantee.
readings.text: [Genesis 32:6] So the messengers returned to Ya‛aqoḇ, saying, “We came to your brother Ěsav, and he also is coming to meet you, and four hundred men with him.” [7] And Ya‛aqoḇ was greatly afraid and distressed. So he divided <dn>את</dn> the people that were with him, and the flocks and herds and camels, into two groups, [8] and he said, “If Ěsav comes to the one group and strikes it, then the other group which is left shall escape.” [9] And Ya‛aqoḇ said, “O <dn>Elohim</dn> of my father Aḇraham and <dn>Elohim</dn> of my father Yitsḥaq, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> who said to me, <dq>‘Return to your land and to your relatives, and <dn>I</dn> do good to you,’</dq> [10] “<dn>I</dn> do not deserve the least of all the loving-commitment and all the truth which <dn>You</dn> have shown <dn>Your</dn> servant, for <dn>I</dn> passed over this Yarděn with my staff, and now <dn>I</dn> have become two groups. [11] “Deliver me, <dn>I</dn> pray, from the hand of my brother, from the hand of Ěsav, for <dn>I</dn> fear him, lest he come and shall strike me and the mother with the children. [12] “For <dn>You</dn> said, <dq>‘<dn>I</dn> shall certainly do good to you, and shall make <dn>את</dn> your seed as the sand of the sea, which are too numerous to count.’ ”</dq>

readings.title: The Economics of Appeasement
readings.subtitle: Ya‛aqoḇ strategically divides his wealth to restore harmony with his brother.
readings.text: [Genesis 32:13] And he spent the night there, and took what came to his hand as a present for Ěsav his brother – [14] two hundred female goats and twenty male goats, two hundred ewes and twenty rams, [15] thirty suckling-camels with their colts, forty cows and ten bulls, twenty female donkeys and ten foals. [16] And he gave into the hand of his servants, every drove by itself, and said to his servants, “Pass over before me, and put some distance between drove and drove.” [17] And he commanded the first one, saying, “When Ěsav my brother meets you and asks you, saying, ‘To whom do you belong, and where are you going? And whose are these in front of you?’ [18] then you shall say, ‘They are your servant Ya‛aqoḇ’s. It is a present sent to my master Ěsav. And see, he also is behind us.’ ” [19] So he commanded the second, and the third, and all who followed the droves, saying, “Speak to Ěsav this same word when you find him, [20] and you shall say, ‘Also look, your servant Ya‛aqoḇ is behind us.’ ” For he said, “Let me appease him with the present that goes before me, and after that see his face. He might accept me.” [21] And the present passed over before him, but he himself spent the night in the camp.

readings.title: Striving with the Right Arm
readings.subtitle: Ya‛aqoḇ wrestles the physical manifestation of Elohim and is marked with a new Shem.
readings.text: [Genesis 32:22] And he rose up that night and took <dn>את</dn> his two wives, and <dn>את</dn> his two female servants, and <dn>את</dn> his eleven sons, and passed over the ford of Yabboq. [23] And he took <dn>את</dn> them and sent them over the stream, and sent over what he had. [24] And Ya‛aqoḇ was left alone. And a Man wrestled with him until the breaking of day. [25] And when <dn>He</dn> saw that <dn>He</dn> did not overcome him, <dn>He</dn> touched <dn>את</dn> the socket of his hip. And the socket of Ya‛aqoḇ’s hip was dislocated as <dn>He</dn> wrestled with him. [26] And <dn>He</dn> said, <dq>“Let <dn>Me</dn> go, for the day breaks.”</dq> But he said, “<dn>I</dn> am not letting <dn>You</dn> go until <dn>You</dn> have blessed me!” [27] So <dn>He</dn> asked him, <dq>“What is your name?”</dq> And he said, “Ya‛aqoḇ.” [28] And <dn>He</dn> said, <dq>“Your name is no longer called Ya‛aqoḇ, but Yisra’ěl, because you have striven with <dn>Elohim</dn> and with men, and have overcome.”</dq> [29] And Ya‛aqoḇ asked <dn>Him</dn>, saying, “Please let me know <dn>Your</dn> Name.” And <dn>He</dn> said, <dq>“Why do you ask about <dn>My</dn> Name?”</dq> And <dn>He</dn> blessed him there. [30] And Ya‛aqoḇ called the name of the place Peni’ěl, “For <dn>I</dn> have seen <dn>Elohim</dn> face to face, and my life is preserved.” [31] And the sun rose on him as he passed over Penu’ěl, and he limped on his hip. [32] That is why the children of Yisra’ěl to this day do not eat the sinew of the hip, which is on the socket of the thigh, because <dn>He</dn> touched <dn>את</dn> the socket of the thigh of Ya‛aqoḇ, in the sinew of the hip.

readings.title: The Reconciliation of Brothers
readings.subtitle: Ěsav runs to embrace Ya‛aqoḇ, accepting his blessing in peace.
readings.text: [Genesis 33:1] And Ya‛aqoḇ lifted <dn>את</dn> his eyes and looked and saw Ěsav coming, and with him four hundred men. And he divided the children among Lě’ah, and Raḥěl, and the two female servants. [2] And he put <dn>את</dn> the female servants and <dn>את</dn> their children in front, and Lě’ah and her children behind, and Raḥěl and Yosěph last. [3] And he himself passed over before them and bowed himself to the ground seven times, until he came near to his brother. [4] And Ěsav ran to meet him, and embraced him, and fell on his neck and kissed him, and they wept. [5] And he lifted <dn>את</dn> his eyes and saw <dn>את</dn> the women and <dn>את</dn> the children, and said, “Who are these with you?” And he said, “The children with whom <dn>Elohim</dn> has favoured your servant.” [6] Then the female servants came near, they and their children, and bowed themselves. [7] And Lě’ah also came near with her children, and they bowed themselves. And Yosěph and Raḥěl came near, and they bowed themselves. [8] Then Ěsav said, “What do you mean by all this company which I met?” And he said, “To find favour in the eyes of my master.” [9] But Ěsav said, “I have enough, my brother, let what you have remain yours.” [10] And Ya‛aqoḇ said, “No, please, if I have now found favour in your eyes, then receive my present from my hand, because I have seen your face like seeing the face of <dn>Elohim</dn>, and you were pleased with me. [11] “Please, take my blessing that is brought to you, because <dn>Elohim</dn> has favoured me, and because I have all I need.” And he urged him, and he took it.

readings.title: Pitching Tents in Sukkoth and Sheḵem
readings.subtitle: Ya‛aqoḇ establishes an altar of exclusive worship in the land of Kena‛an.
readings.text: [Genesis 33:12] And he said, “Let us depart and go, and let me go before you.” [13] But he said to him, “My master knows that the children are weak, and the flocks and herds which are nursing are with me. And if the men should drive them hard one day, all the flocks shall die. [14] “Please let my master go before his servant, and let me lead on slowly according to the pace of the livestock that go before me, and according to the pace of the children, until I come to my master in Sě‛ir.” [15] And Ěsav said, “Please let me leave with you some of the people who are with me.” But he said, “Why this? Let me find favour in the eyes of my master.” [16] And Ěsav returned that day on his way to Sě‛ir. [17] And Ya‛aqoḇ set out to Sukkoth, and built himself a house, and made booths for his livestock. That is why the name of the place is called Sukkoth. [18] And Ya‛aqoḇ came safely to the city of Sheḵem, which is in the land of Kena‛an, when he came from Paddan Aram. And he pitched his tent before the city. [19] And he bought <dn>את</dn> the portion of the field where he had pitched his tent, from the children of Ḥamor, Sheḵem’s father, for one hundred qesitah. [20] And he set up a slaughter-place there and called it <dn>Ěl</dn> <dn>Elohě</dn> Yisra’ěl.

readings.title: The Defilement of Dinah
readings.subtitle: A prince of the land breaches structural harmony by humbling Ya‛aqoḇ's daughter.
readings.text: [Genesis 34:1] And Dinah, the daughter of Lě’ah, whom she had borne to Ya‛aqoḇ, went out to see the daughters of the land. [2] And Sheḵem, son of Ḥamor the Ḥivvite, prince of the land, saw <dn>את</dn> her and took <dn>את</dn> her and lay with her, and humbled her. [3] And his being clung to Dinah the daughter of Ya‛aqoḇ, and he loved <dn>את</dn> the girl and spoke kindly to the girl. [4] And Sheḵem spoke to his father Ḥamor, saying, “Take <dn>את</dn> this girl for me for a wife.” [5] And Ya‛aqoḇ heard that he had defiled Dinah his daughter. Now his sons were with his livestock in the field, so Ya‛aqoḇ kept silent until they came. [6] And Ḥamor, the father of Sheḵem, went out to Ya‛aqoḇ to speak with him. [7] And the sons of Ya‛aqoḇ came in from the field when they heard it. And the men were grieved and very wroth, because he had done a senseless deed in Yisra’ěl by lying with Ya‛aqoḇ’s daughter, which should not be done. [8] But Ḥamor spoke with them, saying, “My son Sheḵem’s being longs for your daughter. Please give her to him for a wife. [9] “And intermarry with us, give us your daughters and take our daughters for yourselves, [10] and dwell with us, and let the land be before you. Dwell and move about in it, and have possessions in it.” [11] And Sheḵem said to her father and her brothers, “Let me find favour in your eyes, and whatever you say to me I give. [12] “Ask of me a bride price and gift ever so high, and I give according to what you say to me, but give me the girl for a wife.”

readings.title: The Deceptive Covenant
readings.subtitle: Ya‛aqoḇ's sons weaponize the sign of the covenant against the Ḥivvites.
readings.text: [Genesis 34:13] But the sons of Ya‛aqoḇ answered Sheḵem and Ḥamor his father, and spoke with deceit, because he had defiled Dinah their sister. [14] And they said to them, “We are not able to do this matter, to give our sister to one who is uncircumcised, for that would be a reproach to us. [15] “Only on this condition would we agree to you: If you become as we are, to have every male of you circumcised, [16] then we shall give our daughters to you, and take your daughters to us. And we shall dwell with you, and shall become one people. [17] “But if you do not listen to us and be circumcised, we shall take <dn>את</dn> our daughter and go.” [18] And their words pleased Ḥamor and Sheḵem, Ḥamor’s son. [19] And the young man did not delay to do this because he delighted in Ya‛aqoḇ’s daughter. Now he was more respected than all the household of his father. [20] And Ḥamor and Sheḵem his son came to the gate of their city, and spoke with the men of their city, saying, [21] “These men are at peace with us, so let them dwell in the land and move about in it. And see, the land is large enough for them. Let us take their daughters for us for wives, and let us give them our daughters. [22] “Only on this condition would the men agree to dwell with us, to be one people: if every male among us is circumcised as they are circumcised. [23] “Their herds and their possessions, and all their beasts, should they not be ours? Only let us agree with them, and let them dwell with us.” [24] And all who went out of the gate of his city listened to Ḥamor and Sheḵem his son; every male was circumcised, all who went out of the gate of his city.

readings.title: The Execution of Retributive Justice
readings.subtitle: Shim‛on and Lěvi extract vengeance, bringing a stench upon their father's household.
readings.text: [Genesis 34:25] And it came to be on the third day, when they were in pain, that two of the sons of Ya‛aqoḇ, Shim‛on and Lěvi, Dinah’s brothers, each took his sword and came boldly upon the city and killed <dn>את</dn> all the males. [26] And they killed <dn>את</dn> Ḥamor and <dn>את</dn> Sheḵem his son with the edge of the sword, and took <dn>את</dn> Dinah from Sheḵem’s house, and went out. [27] The sons of Ya‛aqoḇ came upon the slain, and plundered the city, because they had defiled their sister. [28] They took <dn>את</dn> their flocks and <dn>את</dn> their herds, and <dn>את</dn> their donkeys, and that which was in the city and that which was in the field, [29] and <dn>את</dn> all their wealth. And <dn>את</dn> all their little ones and <dn>את</dn> their wives they took captive, and they plundered <dn>את</dn> all that was in the houses. [30] And Ya‛aqoḇ said to Shim‛on and Lěvi, “You have troubled me by making me a stench among the inhabitants of the land, among the Kena‛anites and the Perizzites. And I am few in number, they shall gather themselves against me and shall strike me, and I shall be destroyed, my household and I.” [31] But they said, “Should he treat our sister like a whore?”

readings.title: Removing the Foreign Mighty Ones
readings.subtitle: Ya‛aqoḇ commands his household to achieve Qadosh before returning to Běyth Ěl.
readings.text: [Genesis 35:1] And <dn>Elohim</dn> said to Ya‛aqoḇ, <dq>“Arise, go up to Běyth <dn>Ěl</dn> and dwell there. And make a slaughter-place there to <dn>Ěl</dn> who appeared to you when you fled from the face of Ěsav your brother.”</dq> [2] And Ya‛aqoḇ said to his household and to all who were with him, “Put away <dn>את</dn> the foreign mighty ones that are among you, and cleanse yourselves, and change your garments. [3] “And let us arise and go up to Běyth <dn>Ěl</dn>, and let me make there a slaughter-place to <dn>Ěl</dn>, who answered me in the day of my distress, and has been with me in the way which I have gone.” [4] So they gave Ya‛aqoḇ <dn>את</dn> all the foreign mighty ones which were in their hands, and <dn>את</dn> all their earrings which were in their ears. And Ya‛aqoḇ hid them under the terebinth tree which was near Sheḵem. [5] And they departed, and the fear of <dn>Elohim</dn> was upon the cities that were all around them, and they did not pursue the sons of Ya‛aqoḇ. [6] And Ya‛aqoḇ came to Luz, that is Běyth <dn>Ěl</dn>, which is in the land of Kena‛an, he and all the people who were with him. [7] And he built there a slaughter-place and called the name of the place <dn>El</dn> Běyth <dn>Ěl</dn>, because there <dn>Elohim</dn> appeared to him when he fled from the face of his brother. [8] And Deḇorah, Riḇqah’s nurse, died, and she was buried below Běyth <dn>Ěl</dn> under the terebinth tree. So the name of it was called Allon Baḵuth.

readings.title: The Covenant Reaffirmed
readings.subtitle: Elohim seals the Shem of Yisra’ěl and guarantees the physical inheritance of the land.
readings.text: [Genesis 35:9] And <dn>Elohim</dn> appeared to Ya‛aqoḇ again, when he came from Paddan Aram, and blessed him. [10] And <dn>Elohim</dn> said to him, <dq>“Your name is Ya‛aqoḇ, your name is no longer called Ya‛aqoḇ, but Yisra’ěl is your name.”</dq> So <dn>He</dn> called his name Yisra’ěl. [11] And <dn>Elohim</dn> said to him, <dq>“<dn>I</dn> am <dn>Ěl</dn> Shaddai. Be fruitful and increase, a nation and a company of nations shall be from you, and sovereigns come from your body.</dq> [12] <dq>“And <dn>את</dn> the land which <dn>I</dn> gave Aḇraham and Yitsḥaq <dn>I</dn> give to you. And to your seed after you <dn>I</dn> give <dn>את</dn> this land.”</dq> [13] And <dn>Elohim</dn> went up from him in the place where <dn>He</dn> had spoken with him. [14] And Ya‛aqoḇ set up <dn>את</dn> a standing column in the place where <dn>He</dn> had spoken with him, a monument of stone. And he poured a drink offering on it, and he poured oil on it. [15] And Ya‛aqoḇ called <dn>את</dn> the name of the place where <dn>Elohim</dn> spoke with him, Běyth <dn>Ěl</dn>.

readings.title: The Birth of Binyamin and the Passing of Raḥěl
readings.subtitle: A son of sorrow becomes the son of the right hand as Raḥěl is buried in Ephrath.
readings.text: [Genesis 35:16] Then they set out from Běyth Ěl. And it came to be, when there was but a little distance to go to Ephrath, that Raḥěl began to give birth, and had great difficulty giving birth. [17] And it came to be, as she was having great difficulty giving birth, that the midwife said to her, “Do not fear, for it is another son for you.” [18] And it came to be, as her life was going out – for she died – that she called <dn>את</dn> his name Ben-Oni. But his father called him Binyamin. [19] So Raḥěl died and was buried on the way to Ephrath, that is Běyth Leḥem. [20] And Ya‛aqoḇ set <dn>את</dn> a standing column on her burial-place, which is the monument of Raḥěl’s burial-place to this day.

readings.title: The Twelve Sons of Yisra’ěl
readings.subtitle: Re’uḇěn brings defilement to the camp, and Ya‛aqoḇ finally reunites with Yitsḥaq.
readings.text: [Genesis 35:21] And Yisra’ěl set out and pitched his tent beyond the tower of Ěḏer. [22] And it came to be, when Yisra’ěl dwelt in that land, that Re’uḇěn went and lay with Bilhah his father’s concubine. And Yisra’ěl heard about it. Now the sons of Ya‛aqoḇ were twelve: [23] the sons of Lě’ah were Re’uḇěn, Ya‛aqoḇ’s first-born, and Shim‛on, and Lěvi, and Yehuḏah, and Yissasḵar, and Zeḇulun; [24] the sons of Raḥěl were Yosěph and Binyamin; [25] the sons of Bilhah, Raḥěl’s female servant, were Dan and Naphtali; [26] and the sons of Zilpah, Lě’ah’s female servant, were Gaḏ and Ashěr. These were the sons of Ya‛aqoḇ who were born to him in Paddan Aram. [27] And Ya‛aqoḇ came to his father Yitsḥaq at Mamrě, or Qiryath Arba, that is Ḥeḇron, where Aḇraham and Yitsḥaq had dwelt.
